To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“Sulfobromophtha-lein (BSP), bilirubin, and tauroursodeoxycholate (TUDC) were found to inhibit binding of the fluorescent dye, fluorescein, to isolated rat liver cell plasma membranes, whereas indocyanine-green (ICG) and bromsulfophthalein-glucuronide (BSP-G) did not.
the binding of organic anions to isolated plasma membranes of hepatocytes was saturable, specific, and reversible, with a Kd of 1.5 ± 0.1 μM.
the binding of BSP to hepatic plasma membranes is saturable and that the binding sites have an apparent molecular weight of 100,000 to 200,000.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the binding of sulfobromphthalein (sodium salt), tautrocholate and bilirubin by isolated hepatic cell plasma membrane vesicles.
the study of the interaction between the plasma membrane of hepatocytes and the bile salt tauroursodeoxycholate (TUDC) in vitro, in an attempt to understand the mechanism of bile salt uptake.
the mechanism of hepatic organic anion transport and its possible relationship to the development of hepatobiliary disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the organic anions BSP, indocyanine, flavaspidate glucaminate and iodipamide glucaminate bind to the same binding site on hepatic cell plasma membrane and that taurocholate and bilirubin do not.
the binding of BSP by the isolated membranes is not specific.
the binding of BSP by isolated hepatic cell plasma mem-branes is specific for the dye, and that the dye is bound in a manner which is consistent with that observed in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the binding of BSP and the other organic anions to the hepatic cell plasma membrane is not the only factor determining the hepatic uptake of these substances.
the binding of BSP to hepatic cell plasma membrane is a saturable process and that the binding is not specific for BSP.
BSP binding by the hepatic cell plasma membrane is not a general property of organic anions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plasma membrane of hepatocytes has a high binding affinity for BSP, which is consistent with the fact that BSP is taken up into hepatocytes in vivo.
